description: Port the Cerberus Claude Code plugin to an Amp plugin using the @ampcode/plugin API while preserving review gates, reviewer orchestration, and command-driven workflows.

userStories.title: Add the production Cerberus plugin entry point
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a real Amp plugin entry point so the migration has a stable place to register commands, hooks, and shared runtime utilities.
acceptanceCriteria: Add .amp/plugins/cerberus.ts with the required Amp experimental header and default export
Register the initial session.start handler and shared plugin root/path resolution helpers
The plugin can resolve bundled prompt files relative to the plugin root
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement review gate storage and locking
userStories.description: As a developer, I want file-backed gate storage keyed by thread and gate ID so Cerberus can safely persist review sessions across turns and restarts.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement thread-scoped active-gate and gate-state persistence under the Cerberus state directory
Gate state stores status, iteration counters, reviewer selection, timestamps, and turn dedupe fields
Implement a lock or lease mechanism that prevents overlapping gate mutations for the same gate
Automated tests cover gate read/write and lock behavior
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Port model selection and review JSON parsing helpers
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the review helper logic in TypeScript so reviewer output and intelligence modes are handled consistently without relying on bash utilities.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement model resolution for fast, smart, and max modes including environment variable overrides
Implement helpers to extract, unwrap, and validate the last JSON object from reviewer output
Automated tests cover malformed wrapper text and model override scenarios
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Implement reviewer process runners
userStories.description: As a developer, I want TypeScript reviewer runners so Cerberus can spawn Codex, Gemini, and Claude reviews in parallel through ctx.$ with predictable timeouts and output capture.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement reviewer runners for codex, gemini, and claude using ctx.$
Reviewer execution supports parallel runs, per-reviewer timeouts, and overall failure reporting
Runner results are written in the structure expected by the gate evaluation flow
Automated tests mock CLI execution and cover success, timeout, and parse-failure cases
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Implement consensus evaluation and review feedback formatting
userStories.description: As a developer, I want consensus and feedback logic in TypeScript so the gate can decide whether to pass, fail, or continue with actionable reviewer feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement majority, all, and any consensus modes for PASS, FAIL, and NEEDS_WORK verdicts
Blocking severity handling distinguishes P0 and P1 findings from non-blocking notes
Review feedback formatter produces markdown suitable for an agent continuation message
Automated tests cover pass, fail, max-round, and mixed-verdict scenarios
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add the review-code command scaffold
userStories.description: As a user, I want a Review Code command in Amp so I can configure a Cerberus review from the command palette without manual file editing.
acceptanceCriteria: Register the review-code command under the Cerberus category
The command collects the required review options through ctx.ui input prompts
Invoking the command creates a new gate and starts the first reviewer run using the selected options
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement the agent.end turn-end gate
userStories.description: As a user, I want Cerberus to intercept review turns at agent.end so failed consensus can continue the thread with review feedback instead of silently stopping.
acceptanceCriteria: The agent.end handler loads the active gate for the current thread and ignores unrelated turns
The handler uses locking plus turn dedupe or equivalent idempotency protection before mutating gate state
Pending reviewer runs wait with a bounded timeout and only advance when results are ready
Failed consensus returns an Amp continue action with formatted review feedback while successful consensus allows completion
Automated tests cover duplicate turns, pending reviewers, pass, and continue flows
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add gate clearing and stale gate recovery
userStories.description: As a user, I want to clear or recover stuck Cerberus gates so abandoned or outdated review sessions do not block later work in the same thread.
acceptanceCriteria: Register a clear-gate command that resolves the active gate and records the reason
Cerberus can detect stale pending gates and surface a recovery or cleanup path
Manual gate resolution leaves the thread in a non-blocking terminal state
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Persist code review scope and archive prior iterations
userStories.description: As a developer, I want each code review session to remember its original scope and archive previous reviewer outputs so later rounds can converge without losing context.
acceptanceCriteria: Persist original code review scope including diff mode, diff target, exclusions, and focus area
Before each new review round, move prior reviewer outputs into an iteration archive directory
Subsequent rounds include the archived context needed for iterative convergence
Automated tests cover scope persistence and archive directory creation
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Register review management tools
userStories.description: As an agent, I want first-class Cerberus review tools so I can spawn reviews, inspect gate status, and resolve gates during automated workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: Register cerberus_spawn_review with validated inputs for review type, reviewers, mode, consensus, and max rounds
Register cerberus_gate_status and cerberus_resolve_gate with outputs that reflect the underlying gate state
Tool execution reuses the shared review gate library rather than duplicating business logic
Automated tests cover tool input validation and happy-path execution
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Implement prompt loading and generation tooling
userStories.description: As an agent, I want Cerberus generation tooling and prompt loading utilities so multi-model spec and plan generation can run from the Amp plugin without bash templates.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement prompt file loading relative to the plugin root for bundled markdown assets
Register cerberus_generate for the initial generator types defined in the migration plan
Template substitution is implemented in TypeScript for the prompts used by the generator flow
Automated tests cover prompt resolution and generator input validation
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Register the remaining Cerberus commands
userStories.description: As a user, I want the rest of the Cerberus review and generator commands available from the Amp command palette so the migrated plugin covers the existing command surface.
acceptanceCriteria: Register review-plan, review-spec, verify-epic, create-spec, create-plan, create-tasks, healthcheck, and architecture-review commands
Each command uses shared input handling and shared orchestration helpers where applicable
Command metadata places all commands under the Cerberus category with accurate descriptions
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add integration coverage for the vertical slice
userStories.description: As a developer, I want integration tests around the review-code flow so the new Amp plugin behavior stays reliable as the rest of the migration lands.
acceptanceCriteria: Add integration tests that cover review spawn, agent.end gating, feedback continuation, fix iteration, and passing consensus
Reviewer subprocesses are mocked so the tests are deterministic and fast
Test coverage includes at least one stale or timeout recovery path
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Document regression comparison against the Claude Code plugin
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a regression comparison between the legacy Claude Code plugin and the new Amp plugin so behavior differences are explicit before rollout.
acceptanceCriteria: Run the same representative review scenarios through both plugins
Document expected upgrades, pending backfills, and true regressions in a comparison artifact
Any remaining true regressions are clearly called out with follow-up work identified
Typecheck passes
